newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electricity seen opening steady to lower.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electricity seen opening steady to lower.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures were expected to open steady to lower Friday, with the market expected to level out from a rise in prices Thursday, industry sources said.
In early over-the-counter discussion, July Palo Verde (PV) was assessed near $31.00 per megawatt hour (MWh) from Thursday's NYMEX July futures close at $31.37 per MWh.
July California Oregon Border (COB) was talked near $23.00 from Thursday's futures close at $23.40 per MWh.
NYMEX electricity futures were said to have closed higher Thursday on strong cash market prices and shortcovering, market sources said.
Physical power prices were strong Thursday, with air conditioning demand expected from hot weather in the Southwest.
For the Southwest in general, temperatures were forecast to run about five degrees F above normal through early next week.
In the Pacific Northwest, temperatures were forecast at three to four degrees above normal for the next several days.

Separately, Arizona Public Service's 1,221 megawatt (MW) Palo Verde 1 nuclear power unit near Phoenix remained off line for repairs Friday morning despite company expectations the unit would resume electricity production Thursday.
Also, the 1,087 MW Diablo Canyon nuclear power unit remained off line for refueling, and was expected to restart this weekend.

In addition to the Palo Verde and Diablo Canyon nukes, several units were expected to return to service by Monday, including a 750 MW unit at Colstrip in Montana, a 750 MW unit at Four Corners in Arizona, a 550 MW unit at Jim Bridger in Wyoming and a 400 MW unit at the Bonanza plant in Utah.
